question: While implementing an agent loop, an engineer is unsure where a tool_result block belongs once a tool finishes executing. Which placement correctly continues the conversation so Claude can incorporate the result into its next round of reasoning?
options: A) Store the tool_result in a separate system-role message positioned before the original user prompt at the start of history
B) Attach the tool_result as metadata on the HTTP request headers rather than as part of the messages array sent to the API
C) Add the tool_result as content inside a new user-role message appended after the assistant message that contained the matching tool_use block
D) Insert the tool_result directly inside that same assistant-role message that originally contained the matching tool_use block, replacing it fully
correct_answers: C) Add the tool_result as content inside a new user-role message appended after the assistant message that contained the matching tool_use block
explanations: Incorrect. Placing the result in a system message ahead of the original prompt misrepresents it as background instruction rather than a response to a specific tool call.
Incorrect. Tool results are part of the conversation content the model reads, not transport-level metadata carried in request headers.
Correct. Tool results are returned as content in a subsequent user-role message, appended after the assistant turn that requested the tool, so Claude can read them on the next call.
Incorrect. Editing the prior assistant message to replace the tool_use block would erase the record of what Claude actually requested, breaking the tool_use/tool_result pairing.
